key_insight: Path to Prevention (P2P) is a platform trial designed to test interventions in early-stage neuronal α-synuclein disease before a clinical Parkinson’s diagnosis; it is not an AI cancer drug discovery study.
clinical_relevance: The trial targets a biologically defined population without functional impairment to evaluate interventions intended to slow disease progression.
method: Phase 2A, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled platform embedded within the observational PPMI cohort.
Enrolls adults aged ≥60 with NSD Stage 2B at approximately 35 sites across North America and Europe.
Each regimen includes 125 active-treatment participants and at least 125 shared placebo controls, with treatment lasting up to 144 weeks.
evidence_signal: This design report provides no efficacy results; primary endpoints assess changes in putamen dopamine-transporter binding and MDS-UPDRS Part III motor scores.
watch_item: Bayesian modeling uses data from non-enrolled PPMI participants, making comparability with trial participants an important consideration.
paper_title: Path to Prevention Platform Trial in Early-Stage Neuronal Alpha-Synuclein Disease: Study Design
